reasoning_summary: BUG_DIFF removes the class's entire distance implementation and leaves only pass; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms that the algorithm's established behavior is no longer provided.
BUG_DIFF removes the assignment of font_style but CODE_CONTEXT_01 still interpolates that variable into every SVG stylesheet; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms the resulting SVG path is broken.

BUG_DIFF treats the newer attrs decorators like legacy decorators and removes their special bare-annotation path; CODE_CONTEXT_01 consequently skips any annotation without a field call, matching TEST_FAILURE_01.
BUG_DIFF catches each download exception and only logs it, allowing fetch_data_files to return despite an incomplete cache; TEST_FAILURE_01 covers the lost failure-reporting behavior.

BUG_DIFF assumes sorting stringified outer items is equivalent to sorting the hashes within each item, and it also drops the prefix from the returned value; both established digest cases fail in TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02.

BUG_DIFF makes a registered error rule stop inheriting SyntaxRule even though its body uses inherited rule state and add_issue behavior shown in CODE_CONTEXT_01; the broad normalizer failure begins with TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF replaces the repository's ${VAR:-default} pattern handling with an unrelated {{VAR}} regex and omits escaped-dollar normalization; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows the actual expansion pattern, and all three affected contracts fail.

BUG_DIFF rewrites write-side completion but drops the required unread-request branch that sets _disconnect_on_finish; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows connection closure depends on that flag, matching both early-return failures.

BUG_DIFF reuses the augmented token such as += for ordinary and reflected binary lookups, while CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows those maps are keyed by + and only the augmented map accepts +=; representative augmented-inference tests fail.

BUG_DIFF assumes QueryBuilder.into is only an INSERT entry point and removes the existing-select branch that sets _select_into; CODE_CONTEXT_01's SQL dispatcher depends on that flag, so all SELECT INTO variants fail.

BUG_DIFF narrows nested-route handling to Mount, drops Host, and removes rebinding to route.routes; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore recurses on the outer list for mounts and omits host-contained endpoints, matching the schema failures.

BUG_DIFF stores change_time on the object before replacing a missing value with the current time, so CODE_CONTEXT_01 leaves self.change_time as None while only last_used receives the normalized timestamp; cache update and pickling paths fail.

BUG_DIFF changes groups from NamedTuple objects to dictionaries but CODE_CONTEXT_02 still serializes each group with _asdict, and it removes both describe_group layers entirely; creation/description and listing tests consequently fail.

BUG_DIFF broadly rewrites unrelated file opening, listing, unset, and run semantics, including several inverted conditions; failures across representative commands show that this excessive cross-command change itself constitutes the defect.

BUG_DIFF retains plugins in APISpec and Components but removes the constructor loop that calls each plugin's init_spec hook; CODE_CONTEXT_01 then uses uninitialized plugins throughout component helpers, producing the broad plugin-dependent failures.

BUG_DIFF moves calculation of expr_stmt below the branch that reads it; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore references an uninitialized local whenever BackslashNode is constructed, breaking multiple normalizer paths.

BUG_DIFF passes a compiled regex through StringMethods.match and relaxes only that accessor's public typing/documentation; CODE_CONTEXT_02 delegates the value unchanged to the backing array, and TEST_FAILURE_01 shows the pyarrow string backend does not accept it.

BUG_DIFF removes the path-separator normalization from matches, although CODE_CONTEXT_01 uses it for filesystem paths; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm that previously supported backslash paths no longer match.

BUG_DIFF assumes a parsed config_file option and calls _run_hydra without its established args_parser argument, replacing the existing experimental_rerun path; CODE_CONTEXT_01 exposes those incompatible API uses and the broad failures include ordinary runs and config-display paths.

BUG_DIFF splits indexed insertion into add followed by conan_api.remotes.move, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 defines no move API and already implements index handling in add; it also drops the force option needed by add's duplicate contract, matching the remote-add failures.

BUG_DIFF rewrites the established MI formula with different comment scaling and clamps the unnormalized value directly, so CODE_CONTEXT_01 no longer returns the repository's promised 0-100 normalized metric; both known-value tests fail.

BUG_DIFF replaces a passing coverage loop with assertions that assume unsupported parse_time and SimpleTZ semantics; CODE_CONTEXT_01 itself shows positive offsets represented with SimpleTZ('01'), not SimpleTZ('+01'), and the rewritten test fails.

BUG_DIFF moves an unconditional return of relative_string ahead of every assignment in ThaiLocale._format_relative; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises on all relative-format paths, as confirmed by the future, now, and past failures.

BUG_DIFF moves direct_url = self.direct_url below the conditional that reads direct_url; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises before either editable-location representation can be resolved, and the frozen-representation test fails.

BUG_DIFF assumes presence of the text key identifies a text frame, but the message contract can carry text=None; both sync and async paths then discard the bytes alternative, and TEST_FAILURE_01 exercises that case.

BUG_DIFF removes millfn's default argument and replaces its established NumOutOfRangeError with the largest known suffix, silently mapping unsupported magnitudes to decillion; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms that public behavior regressed.
BUG_DIFF removes the only assignment to y while CODE_CONTEXT_01 still reads y in the non-haversine distance calculation; TEST_FAILURE_06 confirms that the direct distance behavior now fails.

BUG_DIFF moves the assignments to path and root_path below their first conditional use, and CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises on every get_route_path call; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms the resulting broad routing failure.

BUG_DIFF stops removing deleted assignments and deletes both status-description implementations while returning unrelated response-layer request IDs; the three TEST_FAILURE entries cover deletion and both established status APIs.

BUG_DIFF removes the assignment that extracts fragment from uri but CODE_CONTEXT_01 immediately parses that now-undefined name, and it also suppresses the expires_in integer conversion; TEST_FAILURE_03 confirms implicit-response parsing fails.

BUG_DIFF materializes parse results into an OrderedDict before interpolation, incorrectly collapsing repeated keys that resolve sequentially; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows resolve_variables depends on that stream order, and TEST_FAILURE_01 covers the duplicate-key reference case.

BUG_DIFF weakens the established parser contract by accepting port zero and addresses with multiple colons; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 directly confirm both formerly rejected inputs are now accepted.

BUG_DIFF passes jobs as a local variable even though CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows Stage.run accepts it only through kwargs, so import synchronization reads an undefined name; it also drops no_download output ignoring, and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms remote dependency resolution regresses.

BUG_DIFF deletes inspect and inspect_err from both Result variants, removing public side-effect-preserving operations; all three TEST_FAILURE entries directly exercise the lost methods and their ordinary-call behavior.

BUG_DIFF assigns no multiplier to EPOCH_NANOSECOND and applies 10^9 to the default epoch unit, reversing the units represented by DATE_PART; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows that scale feeds TimeToUnix multiplication and TEST_FAILURE_01 covers timestamp conversion.

BUG_DIFF makes _ignore_ an inferred enum member and removes the standard _name_ and _value_ properties from synthesized members; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 directly confirm both enum behaviors regress.

BUG_DIFF replaces the entire registered-type validator dispatch loop with pass, so CODE_CONTEXT_01 can no longer yield validators for standard modeled types; TEST_FAILURE_03 and TEST_FAILURE_05 confirm existing V1 validation behavior regresses.

BUG_DIFF reverses _extract_metrics' branches, logging valid scalar or nested metrics as unsupported while retaining only None or empty results; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows the inverted collection and the metric-show failures confirm the regression.

BUG_DIFF applies incorrect MIDI byte ordering, includes the status byte instead of excluding it, inverts sysex and validation checks, and extracts the wrong channel bits; the cited failures cover channel, sysex, and encode/decode round trips.

BUG_DIFF removes Nobara from the established DNF distribution mapping, so CODE_CONTEXT_01 can no longer select a default tool for that supported platform; TEST_FAILURE_01 directly confirms the Nobara-to-DNF regression.

BUG_DIFF assumes slice objects can serve as dictionary keys when building patch_lookup, but the runtime used by this code treats them as unhashable; CODE_CONTEXT_01 reaches that construction for every patch build and the replacement and insertion failures confirm it.

BUG_DIFF removes the assignment to uid but CODE_CONTEXT_01 still tests uid for common element names, causing an unbound-local failure; it also drops class and UID description content, and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms normal article processing now fails.

BUG_DIFF moves condition notification after external event signaling in close, changing the established ordering by which blocked readers are released; CODE_CONTEXT_01 documents immediate closed-pipe read semantics and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms a downstream agent read regresses.

BUG_DIFF replaces the token feature names and value formats, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 still feeds those features to the unchanged bundled CRF model trained against the original schema; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms feature behavior, including Unicode handling, is no longer compatible.

BUG_DIFF makes a Lean-specific relocation by deleting the dedicated module, but also replaces every lexer mapping after LilyPond with a placeholder; CODE_CONTEXT_02 additionally uses include without importing it. This excessive collateral rewrite leaves 5,060 failures and no passing tests.

BUG_DIFF removes the administrator-account operation from the backend, response handler, and URL routing layers, eliminating an established API in both configured and empty-account states; the two TEST_FAILURE entries directly cover those lost behaviors.

BUG_DIFF rewrites the general byte-length calculation but drops the YBR_FULL_422 packing correction; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore counts three stored samples where that representation stores two, and TEST_FAILURE_01 through TEST_FAILURE_03 confirm the error across bit depths.

BUG_DIFF removes both the creation of a per-instance Random object and the seeded-state update from seed_instance(); CODE_CONTEXT_01 consequently seeds the shared generator, and TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm regressions in existing seeding behavior.

BUG_DIFF removes ImportFrom's Import superclass even though CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows its methods require the inherited syntax-node state such as children and the parser-node initialization path; TEST_FAILURE_02 and TEST_FAILURE_14 confirm import parsing regressions.

BUG_DIFF removes the pkglist formatter and replaces the command's structured return containing pkglist and reference with a bare reference; CODE_CONTEXT_01 exposes only that reduced contract, and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms the export-to-upload workflow regression.

BUG_DIFF changes the matched shortcode slice from i:j+1 to i:j-1; because Python excludes the upper bound, CODE_CONTEXT_01 now drops the closing token and the token immediately before it, while TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm downstream rendering failures.

BUG_DIFF replaces the shared item reader with a manual parser that compares DicomBytesIO.read_tag() results directly to integer tag literals, while CODE_CONTEXT_01's established reader compares them to ItemTag and SequenceDelimiterTag objects; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_03 confirm that both populated and empty BOT inputs are rejected.

BUG_DIFF assumes entry_points is available from dask.compatibility instead of the repository's dask._compatibility importlib_metadata shim and also reorders an established positional constructor parameter; CODE_CONTEXT_01 contains those incompatible assumptions, and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms backend dispatch no longer preserves its error behavior.

BUG_DIFF deletes the author taxonomy's classification, overview-context, and cross-language-variant hooks; CODE_CONTEXT_01 leaves the plugin unable to supply those established author-page behaviors, and TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm permalink regressions.

BUG_DIFF removes conversion of num1 to float while CODE_CONTEXT_01 still converts num2 and then performs mixed-type addition and subtraction; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm that supported non-float numeric inputs no longer produce the promised distances.

BUG_DIFF reintroduces Bokeh's older plot_height figure attribute, removes the Bokeh-3 compatibility warnings, and stops filtering the non-figure label_size option; CODE_CONTEXT_01 is therefore aligned to an obsolete Bokeh API baseline, and TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms multi-plot failure.

BUG_DIFF rewrites Plane._getrange to call ceil() but does not propagate that dependency to the module imports; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises during routine plane indexing, and TEST_FAILURE_03 and TEST_FAILURE_04 confirm broad layout failures.

BUG_DIFF introduces a frame-depth decorator but does not propagate its requirements: CODE_CONTEXT_01 neither imports wraps nor defines the referenced _with_frame_depth method, and the helper is not integrated with TypeAdapter methods; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm regressions in the class's documented usage.

BUG_DIFF attaches the recursive child-processing block to `not segment.segments` and moves the leaf abort to the opposite branch; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore tries to recurse only for childless segments and skips composites, while TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02 confirm missing source patches.

BUG_DIFF narrows Path.__eq__ to Path instances and deletes the established TType comparison branch; CODE_CONTEXT_01 still constructs Path from TType operations, so equivalent Path and T expressions compare unequal, exactly as confirmed by TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF deletes the assignments that derive expressions and per-expression comments, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 immediately reads both local names throughout Generator.expressions(); TEST_FAILURE_01 through TEST_FAILURE_03 confirm that ordinary, variadic, and nested generation paths now fail.

BUG_DIFF changes three cursor offsets from minus one to minus zero; CODE_CONTEXT_01 consequently advances across the full multi-character delimiter and slices from the wrong current positions, so delimiter text is consumed or included incorrectly, as confirmed by TEST_FAILURE_01's Jinja tokenization failure.

BUG_DIFF reverses the Python-version branches for rebuilding traceback FrameSummary objects: Python 3.11+ loses its enhanced location fields while older versions receive the newer constructor arguments. CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows that this version-dependent reconstruction drives formatted snippet tracebacks, and TEST_FAILURE_01 fails on that behavior.

BUG_DIFF moves `off = self.off` below the `if off is None` check in CT_Transform2D.y, so the getter reads an uninitialized local before it can inspect the transform offset. CODE_CONTEXT_01 confirms the corresponding x getter initializes that local first, and TEST_FAILURE_04 exercises shape-position access.

BUG_DIFF replaces the current UID catalog with an older-style subset: it deletes newer transfer and generated storage UIDs, adds a legacy Python-version alias block, and then still references deleted HTJ2K/JPEG XL names while also using unimported `sys`. CODE_CONTEXT_03 therefore cannot initialize on this repository baseline, consistent with TEST_FAILURE_01 and the entire suite failing at import.

BUG_DIFF moves the return from Request.duplicate_params ahead of both the `seen_keys` initialization and the loop that populates it. CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises on every duplicate-parameter check instead of computing duplicates, and TEST_FAILURE_19 exercises request error handling that depends on this property.

BUG_DIFF assumes FileCheckerManager.is_path_excluded is equivalent to the legacy API's full expand_paths decision. CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows the replacement omits filename-pattern filtering and, when a parent is present, no longer checks the bare filename separately; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms the public excluded() behavior regresses.

BUG_DIFF removes the public `--test-missing` option, its compatibility check, and the binary-state gate that skipped test_package for an already-existing package. CODE_CONTEXT_01 consequently always runs an available test package, and both failing integration tests cover the removed package-only-build behavior.

BUG_DIFF assumes Python 3 WSGI header strings can be returned unchanged and decodes byte values as Latin-1. CODE_CONTEXT_01 documents the actual lossless Latin-1 WSGI representation and elsewhere converts it back through Latin-1 bytes to UTF-8; the replacement therefore preserves mojibake instead of recovering Unicode, as TEST_FAILURE_01 demonstrates.

BUG_DIFF replaces the order-independent absolute time difference with `self.time - track_point.time`, allowing a negative result when the other point is later. CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows speed and missing-speed calculations consume this duration as an elapsed interval, and TEST_FAILURE_03 directly confirms the time-difference contract is broken.

BUG_DIFF assumes the Optional schema object itself is the correct output key for a missing default and assigns `self.key = schema`. CODE_CONTEXT_01 inserts defaults using `new[default.key]`, while Literal.__str__ exposes the actual literal key, so wrapped literals now produce object keys instead of their string value; both default-handling tests fail.

BUG_DIFF adds a special empty-TupleExpr diagnostic and then still runs the normal tuple/list lvalue analysis. That redundant check emits `can't assign to ()` in addition to the established non-iterable error instead of letting the existing analysis own the case; TEST_FAILURE_01 fails on the extra diagnostic.

BUG_DIFF moves the batch-update options out of the request body and passes an unsupported params argument to values_batch_update; TEST_FAILURE_01 exercises Worksheet.batch_update and fails on that client API mismatch.

BUG_DIFF reverses the operands of two percent-format expressions and misorders the file-descriptor range endpoints, reflecting incorrect Python-formatting and closerange assumptions; the four cited spawn/error-path tests fail on those changes.

BUG_DIFF assumes _get_ttype_class is equivalent to _get_css_classes, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows the removed loop intentionally accumulated every parent CSS class; TEST_FAILURE_01 fails when a custom token depends on that hierarchy.

BUG_DIFF inserts an unconditional return ahead of all f-string closing logic, so the tokenizer can never emit a detected FSTRING_END; the cited error-recovery and invalid-f-string tests regress accordingly.

BUG_DIFF removes the path parser's root stripping and state initialization, stops accumulating ordinary path characters, and leaves inside_quotes and brackets undefined; the cited extraction and delta tests show the resulting core path behavior regression.

BUG_DIFF changes X509Extension.__str__ to prepend critical, to the extension text, although CODE_CONTEXT_01 stores criticality separately and the established string contract returns only the rendered value; TEST_FAILURE_01 detects that output regression.

BUG_DIFF moves the _apply return ahead of the local var_func definition, incorrectly assuming that closure can be referenced before its assignment; CODE_CONTEXT_01 makes the resulting unbound local and unreachable variance setup explicit, and the cited var/std tests fail.

BUG_DIFF swaps the MOD 11-2 checksum branches, returning 11 for a zero remainder and 0 for other valid remainders; this contradicts the business-ID data contract documented in CODE_CONTEXT_01 and fails TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF removes the separate empty-size guard, implicitly treating the preceding any(...) character check as sufficient; CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows that check is false for empty bytes, so malformed empty chunk sizes reach int conversion and the two invalid-request tests regress.

BUG_DIFF removes the IoT-specific setup override that forces use_raw_body=True, incorrectly assuming the base response setup is suitable for publish payloads; CODE_CONTEXT_01 then forwards self.body to publish, and TEST_FAILURE_01 fails for the binary-body path.

BUG_DIFF deletes consumption of the repository-specific tools.files.download:verify configuration while CODE_CONTEXT_01 continues to resolve the sibling retry settings from that same configuration before invoking the downloader; TEST_FAILURE_01 confirms the verify configuration contract is violated.

BUG_DIFF reorders the access-token validation pipeline as though its steps were independent, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 now reads valid_client and v before assignment, returns before later checks, and defeats the documented dummy-value sequencing; the cited validation tests fail on that dependency error.

BUG_DIFF replaces the explicit negative-duration prefix logic with a bare strftime call, incorrectly assuming that helper preserves the duration sign; CODE_CONTEXT_01 now has no other sign handling and the cited negative-format tests fail.

BUG_DIFF rewrites dispatch around FileType.VIRTUAL_ENV, REQUIREMENTS, and PYTHON and a different reader, but the repository contract uses VIRTUAL_ENVIRONMENT plus the four concrete lock/manifest types; this false enum/API model breaks the CLI path exercised by TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF moves message_bytes assignment after every use in on_part_data, violating Python's local-variable execution order; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore raises before either size checking or data/file accumulation, as the cited multipart tests demonstrate.

BUG_DIFF replaces the shared validator lookup with a narrower accessor but does not propagate max_digits and decimal_places support, and CODE_CONTEXT_01 calls add_js_update_schema without any definition or import; the constraint refactor is therefore incomplete across its validator and schema representations, preventing even the cited import test from passing.

BUG_DIFF removes the final raw-source slice, incorrectly assuming the patch-derived slices cover the whole file; CODE_CONTEXT_01 builds output only from the returned slices, so any text after the last patch is omitted, exactly as the two slicing tests expose.

BUG_DIFF removes the entire keyword-trie scan from _scan_keywords, leaving word unset and reducing tokenization to single characters or generic variables; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore cannot recognize multi-character comments, strings, operators, or spaced keywords, as the cited tests confirm.

BUG_DIFF assumes every Scope-valued entry in sources is an actual reference, but CODE_CONTEXT_01 distinguishes all available sources from selected_sources that appear in FROM or JOIN; counting availability inflates CTE references and breaks both cited optimizer tests.

BUG_DIFF rewrites dataclass serialization around role_map and class_map, which CODE_CONTEXT_01 shows belong to PDFStructTree rather than PDFStructElement, while omitting the element's actual type, text, page, attributes, and MCID fields; the cited conversion and tree tests fail on that false object model.

BUG_DIFF removes reference resolution for schemas nested under an OpenAPI v3 parameter or header content media type while retaining direct schema and example resolution; TEST_FAILURE_01 shows the schema-reference transformation was no longer propagated to that required representation.

BUG_DIFF replaces merged defaults with explicit keyword arguments followed by engine_kwargs, so a user-supplied duplicate such as data_only or read_only raises instead of overriding the default; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_04 exercise those conflicts.

BUG_DIFF moves the assignment of rels_of_reltype below all of its uses and after an unconditional return, so part_with_reltype fails on an unbound local before it can implement any lookup behavior; TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_03 cover the affected method.

BUG_DIFF removes TypeVar from the typing imports while CODE_CONTEXT_06 still evaluates FILTER_TYPE = TypeVar("FILTER_TYPE") and uses it in several helpers, leaving the typing rollback incomplete and causing the EC2 import path exercised by TEST_FAILURE_01 to fail.

BUG_DIFF removes the ValueError-to-AstroidValueError translation around container slicing; CODE_CONTEXT_01 now applies a zero-step slice directly to elts, allowing Python's raw ValueError to escape in the behavior covered by TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF deletes the generated docstring from the returned decorator and assigns it to new_func instead, immediately before update_wrapper copies metadata from the wrapped callback; CODE_CONTEXT_01 therefore leaves the decorator undocumented, as exercised by TEST_FAILURE_01.
BUG_DIFF removes all explicit type, nonnegative-age, and minimum-versus-maximum validation from date_of_birth, regressing the invalid-input exception behavior exercised by TEST_FAILURE_01.

BUG_DIFF stops find_dotenv from skipping frames whose co_filename does not exist on the filesystem, so CODE_CONTEXT_01 can pass a zip-import pseudo-path to _walk_to_root and break both graceful zip-import behaviors covered by TEST_FAILURE_01 and TEST_FAILURE_02.
